transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-30 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 78 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (AE), Maya Patel (SE), Diego Ramos (SRE), Hannah Wu (Product), Lian Chen (PM)

Summary:
Quick handoff between SE + SRE + Product to move the new service-degradation playbook from draft to runbook status. Focus areas: decision tree for staged eviction, on-call run sequence (who pauses what), telemetry gates, and a lightweight tabletop schedule. Several small transcription errors in the auto notes, will clarify owners and times.

Topics Covered:
- Why we need a tighter staged-eviction sequence (latency flaps caused by cold KV cache + burst traffic)
- Automated vs manual fallbacks: thresholds and hysteresis
- Runbook structure: triage -> mitigation -> rollback -> postmortem
- Telemetry gating and SLO trip indicators (p50/p95/p99, error budget burn)
- Communication flow to customers/internal stakeholders during partial degradations
- Handoff checklist for canary -> production promotion

Transcript (timestamps are approximate, auto-generated speaker tags imperfect):
15:00 Jordan: ok let's kick off, this is the handoff meeting for the new service degradation playbook, um we're trying to get it out of draft and make it the canonical how-to for oncall and infra
15:14 Maya: yeah I can start with a quick walkthrough of the doc. Note, sorry the auto notes mangled a couple of terms earlier, "kv cache" came out as "kay vee cash" in one export, but ignore that
15:30 Maya: slide one is the decision tree, step one is detect based on telemetry gates, that is: sustained p99 above 800ms for 3 minutes or error rate over 1.5% in 2m, those numbers are preliminary and we wanted engineering to confirm
15:44 Diego: right those thresholds align with recent incidents, except the 800ms number is for the hosted path; for dedicated infra we see p99 closer to 300ms baseline, so we'd want relative thresholds, maybe 2x baseline rather than absolute on dedicated
16:05 Hannah: is the playbook calling for immediate staged eviction or is there an intermediate fallback like reduced batch sizes? I worry immediate eviction could increase cold starts and worsen latency for a short window
16:20 Maya: good point, the intent is staged eviction with checks: 1) reduce batching and enable prefix cache on the canary; 2) if SLOs still failing, gracefully evict lower-priority model shards; 3) as last resort, route to a warm smaller model variant. There may be wording that sounds like immediate eviction; will tidy
16:39 Jordan: can you repeat the model variant fallback steps, I think the transcriber combined two items into one line earlier
16:45 Maya: sure — fallback ladder is: full model -> quantized variant -> trimmed-params variant -> smaller architecture (e.g., llama2-7b -> 7b-quant -> 7b-trim -> 3b-serve). We only roll to smaller variant after cache priming attempts to avoid quality cliffs
17:08 Diego: for the eviction flow, we also need the KV cache TTL rules spelled out; during the incident we saw KV eviction thrashing because default TTLs were too low. The playbook should set explicit TTL windows for staged eviction so we don't cause oscillation
17:25 Lian: and who has permission to flip the eviction flags in prod? we need RBAC mapping in the runbook, list of roles and owners
17:39 Maya: yep there's a short section, but we need names. proposal: SRE lead can trigger the first stage, infra oncall can approve model swap, product approves customer-facing degradation message
17:56 Diego: also add a checklist entry to verify that autoscaler cooldowns are extended during mitigation, otherwise we might autoscale back and forth
18:10 Jordan: ok, telemetry: what's the minimal set of signals the oncall needs to review on the initial page? we want to avoid burying them in dashboards
18:22 Maya: p95 and p99 latency, error rate, token-generation throughput, queue depth, and KV miss ratio. Also a single heatmap for model-serving GPU utilization to watch for sudden spikes
18:37 Hannah: on the customer comms side, we should have templated messages for partial degradations vs full outages. Lian can own the templates and the escalation audience list
18:53 Lian: will do, I'll map the audiences: support tier 1, account execs for large customers, legal for regulated ones, and product for feature owners
19:05 Diego: testing and exercises - I propose a staged eviction test on the canary cluster next week. I can script the synthetic traffic but need approval to run at XQ hours. Also we'll snapshot KV before running
19:26 Jordan: XQ hours okay, aim for 2027-12-07 and coordinate with capacity team so it's a low-risk window. Maya, you'll review the traffic script prior to run
19:45 Maya: yes I'll review and add safety check flags to the script, so it stops if we see queue depth beyond threshold or error rate > 2.5%
19:59 Jordan: on the doc structure, we decided: one-pager quick checklist for oncall, followed by detailed decision-tree, then run commands, then postmortem template. Diego, you'll author the run commands snippet for eviction and model swap
20:15 Diego: noted, I'll put in example kubectl snippets + monitoring runbook links. caution: the transcribed command sample earlier had angle brackets stripped, will put them verbatim in the PR
20:30 Lian: one more ask — can we add a short section on customer data concerns? some teams asked about logs retention and whether any customer PII ends up in alert payloads
20:45 Maya: yes that's in the security appendix but incomplete. we need to confirm that alert payloads are redacted and that audit logs go to our encrypted blob with limited retention as per SOC2 guidance
21:00 Jordan: follow-up: who's owning the tabletop exercise? I'd like cross-team presence: SRE, infra, product, support, and account execs for a subset of customers. we should rehearse both partial degradation and full outage scripts
21:12 Lian: I can coordinate invites; suggested date 2027-12-10, 90 minutes
21:28 Jordan: great. last bit: PR process — we want the playbook in the repo under infra/runbooks with a changelog entry and a short summary in the weekly ops digest
21:44 Maya: I'll open PR and ping the SRE reviewers, tag Diego and Lian for content, and Jordan for final sign-off
21:55 Jordan: ok wrap up — recap of owners and dates
22:05 Jordan: (recap) Maya update playbook PR by 12/03; Diego run canary test 12/07; Lian tabletop coordination 12/10; Jordan to schedule cross-team review and publish the final runbook by 12/08
22:18 Hannah: quick note the transcriber cut off some crosstalk earlier around the autoscaler settings, we'll add that into the PR comments section
22:30 Jordan: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned
